rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to evict or not renew
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a written or oral lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds for eviction in court.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant, except hotel and motel guests with no alternate residence who reside there on a continual basis. Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: written Notice to Quit
rules.requirement: Each good cause, except nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail in a written notice to the tenant, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except for nonpayment of rent.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Not required for an eviction for nonpayment of rent.
rules.quoted_span: Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant. A “Notice to Quit” is required for all good cause evictions, except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent ( N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).

rules.title: Eviction ground: failure to pay rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may bring an eviction action for nonpayment of rent without prior notice, except that a 14-day notice is required if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment if the unpaid rent was used to continue landlord-responsible utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) after notice of discontinuance.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: No eviction for nonpayment where the tenant used the unpaid rent to continue utility services the landlord was responsible for and failed to pay.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

rules.title: Eviction ground: disorderly conduct
rules.requirement: If, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood, the landlord may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Eviction ground: damage or destruction to the property
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or by gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage, or injury to the property; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing suit.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Eviction ground: substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: If, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing, the landlord may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing, with notices given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in residential rental properties covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction.
